full_judgment: 16. We may refer to the distinguishing  feature of the case of FM Mohiuddin Rashiduzzaman vs Bahauddin Ahmed 28 DLR (AD) 181 wherein the facts of the case are that a big procession in violation of an Order under section 144 CrPC was brought out. The procession was sought to be dispersed by the police or the EPR by resorting to lathi charge and firing tear gas shells and thereafter when the deceased along with some others were on the footpath, the accused respondent at that moment arrived at the spot on a jeep along with a few other armed constables in the discharge of his duties in the matter of maintenance of law and order. The accused alighted from the jeep with a revolver in hand and proceeded towards the deceased and others forming a cordon and such an action can certainly be related to the duty which the accused was to perform in enforcing the law and order under the aforesaid situation. The action taken by the accused there including firing of shots claimed to have been done in the discharge of his official duty to bring the situation under control and to restore law and order. The Appellate Division held that the respondent accused Bahauddin could not be prosecuted without any sanction as mandated under section 197 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as he could claim that he had acted or purported to act in the discharge of his official duty.
